name: Clayco, Inc.
headquarters: Chicago, Illinois, USA (35 East Wacker Drive; headquarters moved from St. Louis in 2013 — the original St. Louis office at 8640 Evans Avenue remains the registered head office and the larger campus)
founded: 1984 (formed 23 July 1984 in St. Louis by Bob Clark, then 25; Missouri corporation, formerly Clayco Construction Company, Inc.)
employees: 'more than 4,000 employees across the country' (company-overview page, 2026); 'more than 3,800 employees nationwide, with about 1,600 in Chicago' (Chicago Sun-Times, March 2026)

ownership.notes: Privately owned. Founder and executive chairman Bob Clark 'owns most of the company' (Forbes profile, October 2026; net worth USD 7bn, Forbes 400 No. 245); Bloomberg reported in December 2024 that 'Clayco's top executives own 40% of the company' (search snippet of a paywalled article — read as reported). Two executive titles carry 'Shareholder' (CEO Anthony Johnson; Enterprise President and COO Steve Sieckhaus). No ESOP, outside investor or sale process appears in any first-party or credible third-party source. Clayco Compute (January 2025) and Clayco Power & Energy (March 2026) are business units, not legal entities; the operating subsidiaries are LJC (The Lamar Johnson Collaborative, which absorbed Clayco Design & Engineering Inc. in January 2026), Concrete Strategies, Ventana and CRG.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Clayco is the fourth-largest US data-centre builder on the only published ranking — BD+C's 2025 Giants 400 table, USD 3.64bn of 2024 data-centre revenue behind HITT (USD 6.74bn), Holder (USD 6.48bn) and DPR (USD 3.65bn), USD 30m ahead of Turner — and it is converting a vertically integrated design-build model (in-house architecture and engineering, self-performed concrete, enclosure, mechanical and electrical) into a data-centre franchise that Forbes reports will be 75% of nearly USD 12bn of 2026 revenue. The counter-fact is Galaxy Digital's decision to move Helios Phase 2 (260 MW) to HITT in 2026, citing Clayco's 'project commitments' and labour. BACKGROUND. Chicago-based, founded 1984 in St. Louis by Bob Clark, who still owns most of it; CEO Anthony Johnson since January 2025. ENR 2026 Top 400 No. 20 on 2025 revenue of USD 8.1bn (No. 21 and USD 6.8bn a year earlier); No. 1 on BD+C's 2026 design-build list and No. 5 on ENR's, both at USD 7.05bn of design-build revenue. Clayco Compute, the mission-critical unit launched January 2025 under Ryan McGuire, reports 72 active data-centre projects, '10.20GW' delivered or underway and USD 42bn of mission-critical revenue delivered or underway; named live campuses are Galaxy's Helios Phase 1 (133 MW critical IT for CoreWeave, complete July 2026), Related Digital's Cheyenne campus (construction manager, 88 MW of up to 302 MW, CoreWeave anchor) and the PsiQuantum-anchored Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park. Clayco Power & Energy (March 2026) adds solar and BESS EPC with a USD 300m revenue target for 2027, and CRG, the development arm, is pursuing a USD 6bn, roughly 600 MW campus at Festus, Missouri that has already cost the city council its majority. Collection gap: fully private — no audited revenue, margin or backlog; the company's own 2025 revenue boilerplate reads USD 7.6bn in January–March 2026 releases and USD 8.1bn from June 2026, and its 'Top 3 ENR data center contractors' claim could not be matched to any ENR table.
ecosystemRole: We assess Clayco as an incumbent of the EPC-and-construction segment on the ranking the segment's other GC incumbents cite — fourth on BD+C's 2025 data-centre table, within USD 10m of DPR and ahead of Turner, Whiting-Turner and Mortenson — and the most vertically integrated of them: it owns the architect (LJC), the concrete and enclosure subcontractors and a mechanical-electrical self-perform arm (Clayco SEI), and it develops campuses through CRG. In this corpus it is a procurement channel for generators, chillers and power assemblies on the campuses it builds (more than 100 integrated power assemblies and 90 chillers at Helios), a prospective BESS buyer through Clayco Power & Energy, and a developer counterparty at Festus; the equipment it furnishes versus what owners furnish is not disclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Clayco Compute — mission-critical design-build and construction management
productsAndServices.category: Data-centre general contracting · the growth franchise
productsAndServices.description: The mission-critical business unit launched 2025-01-15 under Ryan McGuire, 'focused on hyperscale, cloud, AI-ready, colocation, and enterprise data centers', handling 'site selection, utility strategy, architecture and engineering, procurement, vendor management, off-site modular construction, self-perform concrete, mechanical and electrical systems, integrated quality and commissioning'. Company metrics (undated page, read October 2026): 72 active data-centre projects; '10.20GW' of data-centre density delivered or underway (Bob Clark's August 2026 split: about 2.2 GW completed, more than 8,000 MW under construction); USD 42bn of mission-critical revenue delivered or underway; EMR 0.46. Data-centre revenue was USD 3.6bn in 2024 — 'half of our total revenue and more than double 2023's $1.5 billion' (company) and USD 3.64bn on BD+C's 2025 table; Forbes reports 75% of nearly USD 12bn in 2026.
highlights: Galaxy Digital Helios, Afton TX — general contractor for Phase 1: 133 MW critical IT (about 200 MW gross) of liquid-cooled capacity for CoreWeave on a former 180 MW bitcoin site, complete July 2026; 'more than 100 integrated power assemblies and more than 90 chillers', an on-site batch plant and 'significant off-site assembly' (company). Phase 2 (260 MW) went to HITT in 2026 — Galaxy: 'given their project commitments and our timeline requirements and the necessary labor and workforces'

Related Digital Cheyenne, WY — construction manager for Phase 1: 184,000 sq ft, 88 MW of critical IT anchored by CoreWeave, of a USD 1.2bn, up-to-302 MW campus on 115 acres with Black Hills Energy; first building late 2026 (Related, 2025-10-07)

Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park, Chicago — general contractor for phase 1 of the 128-acre PsiQuantum-anchored campus (LJC designer; CRG co-developer with Related Midwest; groundbreaking 2025-09-30; first unit online 2026)

Microsoft Elk Grove Village campus named by Crain's among the 57 active projects (January 2025); Forbes names Amazon, Microsoft and Oracle as clients; DCD relayed a company list of Microsoft, Amazon, Google, NTT, QTS, Stream, CyrusOne, Stack, Equinix and Prologis

Deep Atomic consortium — Clayco provides 'early-stage delivery planning, constructability analysis, and integrated design-build expertise' for a proposed nuclear-powered AI data-centre campus at Idaho National Laboratory (60 MW MK60 small modular reactors; DOE proposal pending)
productsAndServices.positioning: Fourth on BD+C's 2025 data-centre ranking (USD 3.64bn of 2024 revenue) — behind HITT, Holder and DPR, ahead of Turner, Whiting-Turner, Fortis, JE Dunn and Mortenson; No. 1 on BD+C's and No. 5 on ENR's 2026 design-build lists. Differentiation is vertical integration — architect, engineers, concrete, enclosure and an MEP self-perform arm under one owner — and speed of design-build delivery; the company's 'Top 3 ENR data center contractors' claim could not be matched to an ENR table, and the Helios Phase 2 loss shows capacity is the constraint HITT exploited.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Design-build and construction-management contracts with data-centre owners and developers (Galaxy, Related Digital, Related Midwest/CRG) and hyperscalers; on Helios 'under a construction management structure' with more than 100 subcontractors
targetSegments: Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle named by press)

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess that Clayco's data-centre position rests on vertical integration rather than on speed or scale: it is the only top-five BD+C builder that owns its architect, its concrete and enclosure subcontractors, an MEP self-perform arm and a development company. Basis: BD+C No. 4 (USD 3.64bn) and No. 1 design-build (USD 7.05bn); LJC absorbed engineering in January 2026; CRG develops powered land. The model sells single-source responsibility to owners who want one neck to wring.

2. (High confidence) We assess that labour capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint. Basis: Galaxy moved Helios Phase 2 (260 MW) to HITT citing Clayco's 'project commitments' and 'the necessary labor and workforces'; Power & Energy targets nearly 1,000 new craft by 2027; a President of Self Perform was created in January 2026; ENR's 2026 report describes the whole Top 400 hitting a 'craft ceiling'. A GC that cannot staff a doubled follow-on phase will lose share to HITT and DPR on the largest campuses whatever its ranking.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess that the company's revenue figures are directionally right and specifically unreliable. Basis: 2025 revenue is USD 7.6bn in January–March 2026 releases, USD 8.1bn from June 2026 and USD 8.1bn on ENR's 2026 list, while an August 2026 release labels USD 8.1bn as 2024; Bob Clark's blog cites 'sales to $9 billion in 2024'. Treat any single Clayco revenue number as a boilerplate value, and prefer the ranker's figure with its basis stated.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess that CRG's Missouri campaigns are a strategic liability for the construction business. Basis: St. Charles withdrawn under 6,000 signatures and a moratorium; Festus approved then met with a council wipe-out and a Sunshine-Law suit; Bob Clark's August 2026 essay titled the problem 'trust'. A GC whose affiliate is the face of local opposition carries reputational risk into every Midwestern campus bid, including the hyperscalers' own.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess that the AESC stall is the realised version of the policy-concentration risk Bloomberg flagged in December 2024. Basis: a USD 1.6bn EV-battery plant suspended at 75% complete with more than USD 1bn performed and Clayco paying subcontractors from its own funds; the USD 26.2m lien suit covers only the unpaid tail. A private balance sheet that absorbs owner defaults on industrial-policy projects is the under-reported exposure behind the data-centre growth story.

6. (Low confidence) We assess that Clayco Power & Energy will first serve Clayco's own data-centre clients rather than utilities. Basis: the release names 'data center operators' among target clients and the only project is a confidential Illinois PV-plus-BESS job; the hire of a former Signal Energy president suggests utility-scale ambition. Whether the unit becomes a meaningful BESS buyer depends on one named award — none exists yet.

policyExposure.exposure: CRG's USD 1bn St. Charles campus was withdrawn on 2025-08-18 and the city passed a one-year moratorium, later weighing a permanent ban (May 2026). Festus approved CRG's USD 6bn agreement 6–2 on 2026-03-30; a week later four council incumbents lost to anti-data-centre candidates and a 12-count Sunshine-Law and spot-zoning suit was filed against the city and CRG Acquisition LLC.
policyExposure.mitigation: Community-benefit terms in the Festus agreement (USD 3m a year for five years, then USD 5m; water, sewer and street upgrades) and Bob Clark's stated reliance on 'vested rights' to break ground.

policyExposure.regime: DOE federal-site AI data-centre and nuclear co-location initiative
policyExposure.exposure: Clayco is the constructor in the Deep Atomic-led consortium proposing a nuclear-powered AI data-centre campus at Idaho National Laboratory (MK60 60 MW small modular reactors), submitted to DOE's Office of Nuclear Energy at the end of 2025 under the 2025 federal-sites programme. No award has been reported.

policyExposure.regime: Federal EV and battery manufacturing incentives (IRA)
policyExposure.exposure: AESC suspended its USD 1.6bn Florence, South Carolina battery plant on 2025-06-08 citing 'policy and market uncertainties' with Clayco's design-build about 75% complete; Clayco sued for USD 26.2m of unpaid work in July 2026 after paying its subcontractors from its own funds. Rivian's Georgia plant, also Clayco's, paused in 2024 and resumes in 2026.
